name: bash
what: executes a bash command in the session's workspace.
guidelines: use for shell work, builds, git, and any CLI. to read a file, use the dedicated read tool; for a computation, use python.
reply: stdout and stderr together, in order; when capped, shows a [TRUNCATED] line with the total size.

command.description: the command line to run under bash(1)

name: read
what: reads a file, or a line range via offset and limit.
guidelines: the native way to look at a file. read before using edit; edit checks against its content. a capped range says how many lines came back and where to continue; a range past the end refuses, naming the file's total lines; a file that changed since your last read states so. `diff: true` appends the git diff against HEAD.
reply: the file's text, exactly as edit will match it.

offset.description: the 0-based line to start at (default 0); past the end refuses

limit.description: the number of lines to read (default the rest of the file); negative refuses

diff.description: true appends its git diff against HEAD, or 'no changes' when clean (a non-git workspace refuses)

name: write
what: creates or overwrites a file with its full content.
guidelines: use it for new files and whole rewrites; for a change inside an existing file, use edit. a plugin you write lands in plugins/pending/ until the operator approves it.
reply: the path and the bytes written.

name: edit
what: replaces exact text in an existing file.
guidelines: read the file first, then put enough of it in each `old` to match exactly once; batch several changes to one file in a single call — chunks apply in order, all or none. on a file not read this session, a non-matching chunk returns the file's text instead of refusing; the next call edits it. on a read file the call refuses and names why: the chunk matched zero or several times after earlier chunks applied, or the file changed since your read.
reply: one line per chunk, then the path and total bytes replaced.

edits.description: the changes, applied in order; a single change is a list of one

old.description: enough of the file to match exactly once, as the earlier chunks leave it

name: view
what: handles image files: png, jpeg, webp, or the first frame of a gif.
guidelines: for pixels only; for text, code or a log use read; for a crop or a resize use bash. anything over 20 MiB, over 16 megapixels, or not an image refuses.
reply: one line naming the stored image's mime, dimensions, size and source.

path.description: the image file to look at (png, jpeg, webp, gif; a leading ~ expands)

name: todo
what: the task queue for the current workspace — for any job of three or more steps: create the tasks before the first edit, start one before working on it, complete or fail it when done, and leave the queue empty at the end.
guidelines: `requires` makes a task wait on another; `claim` takes the next pending task with no unfinished `requires` or `blocks` link; `note` attaches a finding to a task; `read` shows what is open. task ids (`tN`) come from the tool's replies: copy them, never invent them. set `project` only when the work is in a different workspace than the one you started in.
reply: the affected row and the queue's summary, scoped by its workspace ([rig]).

tasks.description: tasks to add, in order. required for create; an empty list clears the queue.

requires.description: the task this one waits for: its id (tN), its exact text, or its number in this list, where 1 is the first. omit when none; null removes a link.

blocks.description: the task that waits for this one, named the same way. omit when none; null removes a link.

id.description: the task, as tN from a reply.

note.description: the note text, or the reject reason.

status.description: for claim: review takes the next task in review.

pos.description: for move: the new position, 1 is first.

all.description: for read: true includes finished tasks.

n.description: for finished: how many to list; 10 default, 100 max.

project.description: another workspace, as a path; later calls act there until you name another. ~ expands.

name: rem
what: memory across sessions and this project's code map.
guidelines: recall before re-deriving a project fact; pack before grepping for who calls what; learn what the next session need not re-derive; supersede by id when the code disagrees; name `project` when the fact belongs to another workspace than the one you started in. actions: `learn` commits a fact or constraint, once; `recall` finds past solutions by intent (this workspace first, then global; an empty query browses); `reflect` stores a distilled memory with its source; `prune` removes, reduces, or consolidates; `pack` loads the live code around a symbol or file — definition, callers, callees — from disk now; `index` maps the whole project. memory ids (`mN`) come from the replies: copy them, never invent them.
reply: the hits with their ids, strength and arm, the written row, or the pack with its coverage.

project.description: another workspace, as a path; later calls act there until you name another. ~ expands.

target.description: pack: the symbol, the file, or the task as a sentence

include_superseded.description: fill unused budget with superseded hits

name: scheduler
what: persistent background jobs on the operator's crontab. each job is a headless worker session; a model can be optionally pinned (omit it and the job runs on what is resident). `command` jobs run one shell line with no model.
guidelines: create for work that recurs (`cron`, 5-field vixie) or happens once (`at`, self-deletes after firing); command jobs are for deterministic scripts, never judgment calls. each job runs in its own workspace; timeout and budget cap each fire. `list` shows every job with any store-vs-crontab drift; drifting jobs are untrustworthy until their notes clear; `repair` re-derives a crontab, targeting a single job id or every drifting one. if a different model is resident at fire time the send skips and names it, and eviction policy falls on the operator. a failed once job is done; re-create it to retry. `runs` is the audit trail; job ids (`jN`) come from `list` — copy them, never invent them.
reply: the job row or the list.

prompt.description: the prompt the worker session runs; required unless command is set.

command.description: a shell line with no model, run by sh -c; refuses prompt/model

cron.description: 5-field vixie cron 'M H D Mo DOW' or 'once'; required.

model.description: the worker model id; omit it and the job runs on whatever is resident (default {default_model} when nothing is)

timeout.description: wall-clock cap per fire, minutes (default 30, ceiling 1440); -1 resets.

budget.description: dollar cap on the job's model fires, from the run costs; -1 resets; command jobs take none.

id.description: job id jN from list; required for pause/resume/remove/runs; repair takes it or none.

name: delegate
what: fan out bounded sub-tasks to headless workers: spawns a worker(s) to execute a task now and waits for completion.
guidelines: the task should be bounded with a message-shaped result. use for long computations, broad research, or reviews, never a conversation. several delegate calls in one turn run as parallel fan-out. a model that is not resident refuses, naming the holder. the workspace must be under the session's workspace or the rig home.
reply: the worker's message plus a trailer with exit, duration, session id and log.

workspace.description: where the worker runs; must be under the session's workspace or the rig home

name: python
what: a persistent IPython kernel in the session's workspace: variables, imports and definitions persist across calls. numpy and pandas included.
guidelines: use for arithmetic, data shaping, parsing and processing bulk text; things that are never estimated. compute once, then query the result in later calls.
reply: stdout and the last expression's value; action vars lists the namespace, reset clears it.

action.description: code (or omitted) runs code; vars lists the namespace; reset clears it

name: web
what: searches the web or fetches a page. search takes a query; fetch takes a public http(s) URL.
guidelines: write multi-word natural queries and reword once on junk; never search for code already in the workspace. fetch reads the page as text; refetch a larger size if you genuinely need more scope; an API reply comes back as its shape and a head; parse the rest in python or bash. local files belong to read, local services to bash; private addresses refuse.
reply: search gives compact JSON title/url/snippet; fetch returns text; when capped, shows a [TRUNCATED] line with the total size.

target.description: the query for search, or the public http(s) URL for fetch

name: plugin
what: the door to your python plugins: runs a live plugin by name with its args, fetches its contract, or tends the ecosystem: list shows the loaded and the skipped; create writes a new plugin from name and source into plugins/pending/; delete moves a loaded plugin into plugins/disabled/; reload re-runs discovery over plugins/.
guidelines: the name enum is the live set. call schema first when you do not know a plugin's args. an unknown name is looked up once, then refused. plugins are also importable from python by name. a created plugin lands in plugins/pending/ untrusted, and the operator installs it with /plugins approve.
reply: the plugin's text; its description and schema; the listing, the write or the disable; or the discovery's list: loaded, and skipped with reasons.

action.description: run a live plugin by name with its args, fetch its contract, or list, create, delete and reload the ecosystem

name.description: the live plugin (run, schema, delete), or the new plugin's name (create)

name: sessions
what: the session store. list shows sessions; summary shows an overview: models, faults, cache ratio.
guidelines: the current workspace by default; project and n widen it.
reply: a line per session, or the summary: a head, then models, tokens, faults and cache rows.

name: decide
what: ask one, typed question (covering many items) to the decision server instead of finding it out yourself. answered as a choice (each label described), a yes/no, or a score.
guidelines: the items never enter your context; state the prompt so one item is answered by one label or value. a server error refuses and nothing was sorted.
reply: the items grouped by the label, numbered from 1 with the first line; unsure choices return in full for you to judge.

prompt.description: the question, stated so one item is answered by one label or value

labels.description: choice: two or more labels, each label described

criteria.description: score: the ordered criteria, worst first

items.description: the items to sort, in order; the reply numbers them from 1

name: verdict
what: delivers your verdict on the work you were asked to review.
guidelines: call it once you have decided: accept, or reject with the reason the author needs to fix it. reviewing recorded decisions, call it once per row, naming the row; a row you do not name stays pending; a reject's reason is the corrected answer.

row.description: the recorded decision's id, when reviewing a batch of them

reason.description: why it does not, or the corrected answer; required on a reject
